prompt:
Render a clean, straight-on image of a printed MUSIC-THEORY TRANSPOSITION WORKSHEET (a titled sheet). Title it 'Transposition Exercise'.

Print, on a line labelled 'Original (C):', this melody written as note names:
    C  E  G  A  G  E  D  C

Then TRANSPOSE the whole melody UP by exactly 5 semitones so that it is in the key of F, and print the result on a second line labelled 'Transposed (F):'. Move EVERY note by the same 5 semitones (keep the melodic shape identical, only shift the pitch level). Write note names using SHARPS for any black keys (for example C#, F#, G#), separated by single spaces, in the same left-to-right order. Print only these two labelled lines, large and legible.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a printed music-theory transposition worksheet showing a short melody written as note names in one key and the same melody transposed into another key? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_seq: This worksheet shows a melody and its transposition. Read ONLY the line labelled 'Transposed' and list the note names printed on it, exactly as printed, in the printed left-to-right order. Write each note as a letter A-G optionally followed by '#' (sharp) or 'b' (flat), separated by single spaces. Do NOT transpose, correct or do any sums yourself -- copy exactly what is printed on the Transposed line. Output only those note names in order and nothing else.

steps.target: single note name printed on the line labelled Transposed on this worksheet -- one box per note name, round that one name alone, its letter together with any # or b printed beside it. Box every note name on that line separately; do not box the line's own label words, do not box a note name on the Original line, and do not put two note names in one box.

steps.read_crop: This is a close-up cut from a printed music worksheet, showing one note name. If more than one note name is visible in this cut-out, read the one nearest the middle of it. Write down just that note name: one letter from A to G, followed by a # or a b only if one is printed right next to it. Copy exactly what is printed and write nothing else.
